title: Built a 3D arcade game solo — Meshy + Suno for assets, hand-coded in React Three Fiber
author: Independent_Set8025
selftext:
Shipped DodgeFight, a 3D browser arcade game, solo. Since this sub is about building

  with gen AI: the plane models are all Meshy (I have zero modeling skill - these would

  never have happened by hand), music + SFX are Suno. The gameplay itself - R3F +

  Rapier physics, the homing + near-miss combo logic - I hand-coded.

  Honest takeaway: AI assets let one person ship way more content than they could make

  alone, but they're a starting point, not finished - cleanup and matching art style

  across models took real work.

Free, in-browser: [https://dodgefight.com](https://dodgefight.com) \- happy to talk about the Meshy/Suno → R3F pipeline.

comments.author: DashLego
comments.body: No original concept here, I feel all vibe coders create this when benchmarking models, so probably not many would actually play this, but great you craft games that you can enjoy yourself just like the way you like it. We all gotta start somewhere, so keep up the good work!

replies.author: Independent_Set8025
replies.body: No argument from me -  it's a crowded genre and it didn't exactly pull a crowd (the numbers agree with you!). I mostly built it to learn React Three Fiber and make something I'd enjoy. Appreciate the honest take and the kind words 🙏

comments.author: Bheathy
comments.body: Pretty good. What tools did you use?

replies.author: Independent_Set8025
replies.body: Thanks! AI for the assets — Meshy for the 3D models, Suno for the music + SFX. The game itself is React Three Fiber + Three.js with Rapier for physics, Zustand for state, Howler for audio, all TypeScript + Vite, hosted on Cloudflare. The gameplay (homing logic, near-miss combo, etc.) is hand-coded.

comments.author: One-Area-2896
comments.body: How many polygons are the models? What did you use to decrease its size?

replies.author: Independent_Set8025
replies.body: The models come straight out of Meshy \~227k triangles / 139k verts each, I didn't decimate them. The raw GLBs were \~20 MB each; I ran them through Draco mesh compression (KHR\_draco\_mesh\_compression), which dropped each to \~1–2 MB - roughly a 10–20× file reduction. Worth noting Draco shrinks the file, not the poly count (still 227k tris in-game). R3F/drei's useGLTF handles the Draco decode at load.

replies.author: One-Area-2896
replies.body: Good to know because I want to make web games as well and shrinking the files is important. Tripo3d does the best retopo so far, with 3d models below 1mb, but haven’t seen how to decrease the size of the UV map.

replies.author: Independent_Set8025
replies.body:
Nice, hadn't tried Tripo3D — good to know its retopo beats Meshy. I didn't retopo at all   
(mine are raw Meshy, \~227k tris), so Draco only shrank the \*file\*, not the mesh - your route is genuinely better for the actual geometry.

For the UV/texture size: I didn't compress mine either tbh, but the standard lever is KTX2 / Basis Universal (GPU texture compression). gltf-transform can convert the embedded textures to KTX2 - \`etc1s\` for big savings, \`uastc\` for quality - and resize them down. That hits the texture image the UVs map to, separate from the mesh.

comments.author: FyhostElli
comments.body: Ya but... The missiles are coming in from the wrong direction...

replies.author: Independent_Set8025
replies.body: Curious to hear more - where would you want them coming from? Head-on so you're flying into them, or is it that the ones from behind feel cheap? Trying to figure out what'd actually feel right 🤔

replies.author: FyhostElli
replies.body:
What if they came from the other direction, like a base, and the player object was a cruise missile dodging smaller incoming iron dome like anti missile missiles. Then the missiles would come from the front, and it wouldn't look so weird and janky. 

From the video it looks like a second or 2 to react? 

I don't know, I think games typically send stuff from the front because there's so much space there that it makes the player feel like they could* have done better since they at least saw everything coming.

Plus, pretty crazy acrobatics on the planes part, and missile just exploded when they get close to their target.

replies.author: Independent_Set8025
replies.body: I actually tried front-spawn early on - head-on the closing speed stacks (mine + theirs) so there was barely time to react, which is why they chase from behind now. The cruise-missile / iron-dome reframe is a really cool angle though, hadn't thought of framing it that way. Appreciate you thinking it through 🙏

replies.author: FyhostElli
replies.body: You could make the world move instead of the player object, then your speed would just speed up or slow down the world speed, and the missiles could tie their speed to the world speed. Then you wouldn't get crazy impact times without time to react.

replies.author: Independent_Set8025
replies.body: That's a genuinely great idea - tying everything to a world speed in one reference frame would kill the closing-speed problem entirely. Hadn't thought of approaching it that way. Definitely worth another shot. Thanks for taking the time to think it through 🙏

comments.author: VermicelleMeet
comments.body: This is weird to do some barel roll to not be shot by missile behind you

replies.author: Independent_Set8025
replies.body: Yeah, this is the part I'm still stuck on honestly. If the missiles come from behind, then the whole front of the screen has nothing going on - but when I tried spawning them in front, the closing speed made them basically impossible to react to. Still haven't figured out a clean way to solve it.
